chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The two ears are not from the face, nor from the head. He said, And the wiping was mentioned, so he said: Wipe upon the front of your head, and wipe upon the two feet, and begin with the right side.
ai.seo_question: How should one wipe the head and feet during wudu according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the specific anatomical boundaries for wiping (masah) during ablution, distinguishing the ears from the face and head to prevent over-expansion of the wiped areas. It provides the practical methodology for performing wudu by specifying the front of the head and both feet, with a prescribed order starting from the right, reflecting the Shia emphasis on following the Imams' detailed instructions. This clarification is crucial for understanding the distinction between Shia and Sunni fiqh regarding the extent of wiping versus washing the feet.
